title: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart
body:
Read the chapter → [Psalms 9](/bible/psalms/9)

**[Psalm 9:1-4](/bible/psalms/9#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/9#v1)</sup> I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/9#v2)</sup> I will be glad and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/9#v3)</sup> When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/9#v4)</sup> For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right.

- David praises the Lord with his whole heart and shows forth all his marvelous works, glad and rejoicing in the Most High. When his enemies are turned back, they fall and perish at God's presence, for the Lord sits on the throne judging right.
- Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. Even the Romans who pierced him will be back on the scene and will wail because of him.
  - **[Revelation 20:11](/bible/revelation/20#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/revelation/20#v11)</sup> And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.

    A great white throne, and from the face of him that sat on it the earth and heaven fled away.
  - **[Revelation 1:6-7](/bible/revelation/1#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/revelation/1#v6)</sup> And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/revelation/1#v7)</sup> Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.

    He has made us kings and priests; he comes with clouds, and every eye shall see him, even they that pierced him.

**[Psalm 9:5-8](/bible/psalms/9#v5)**
> <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/9#v5)</sup> Thou hast rebuked the heathen, thou hast destroyed the wicked, thou hast put out their name for ever and ever.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/9#v6)</sup> O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/9#v7)</sup> But the Lord shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/9#v8)</sup> And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

- God rebukes the heathen, destroys the wicked, and puts out their name forever and ever, exactly as Obadiah described. Destructions come to a perpetual end and their cities and memorials perish with them.
- Their memorials are the confederate statues, the presidents' statues, Mount Rushmore with the so-called founding fathers. The Lord will destroy those memorials; in the kingdom you will not remember America.
- The Lord endures forever and will judge the world in righteousness and minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

**[Psalm 9:9-12](/bible/psalms/9#v9)**
> <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/9#v9)</sup> The Lord also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/9#v10)</sup> And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/psalms/9#v11)</sup> Sing praises to the Lord, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the people his doings.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/psalms/9#v12)</sup> When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble.

- The Lord is a refuge for the oppressed in times of trouble, and those who know his name trust in him, for he does not forsake those who seek him. When he makes inquisition for blood he remembers them and does not forget the cry of the humble.
- The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. All we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed.
  - **[Revelation 13:10](/bible/revelation/13#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/revelation/13#v10)</sup> He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.

    He that kills with the sword must be killed with the sword; here is the patience and faith of the saints.
  - **[Revelation 11:18](/bible/revelation/11#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/revelation/11#v18)</sup> And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come, and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great; and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.

    The nations were angry and God's wrath is come to reward the prophets and saints and destroy them who destroy the earth.
  - **[Revelation 18:24](/bible/revelation/18#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/revelation/18#v24)</sup> And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.

    In her (America) was found the blood of prophets and saints and all that were slain upon the earth.
  - **[Zechariah 2:7-8](/bible/zechariah/2#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/zechariah/2#v7)</sup> Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/zechariah/2#v8)</sup> For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.

    Deliver yourself, O Zion, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon; he that touches you touches the apple of God's eye.

**[Psalm 9:15-17](/bible/psalms/9#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/psalms/9#v15)</sup> The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/9#v16)</sup> The Lord is known by the judgment which he executeth: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/psalms/9#v17)</sup> The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God.

- The heathen are sunk down in the pit they made, and in the net they hid their own foot is taken; the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Their own traps set for us take them.
- The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God. They forgot that there is a God in heaven who will redeem the Israelites, and they touched the apple of his eye when they consulted against us.

**[Psalm 9:18-20](/bible/psalms/9#v18)**
> <sup>[18](/bible/psalms/9#v18)</sup> For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/psalms/9#v19)</sup> Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail: let the heathen be judged in thy sight.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/psalms/9#v20)</sup> Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.

- The needy shall not always be forgotten and the expectation of the poor shall not perish. David prays the Lord to arise, let the heathen be judged, and put them in fear so the nations know themselves to be but men.
- The nations have reigned so long that in their minds they think they are God. David prays that the Lord remind them they are nothing but men; the only reason they could do what they did to us is that we broke God's laws.
  - **[Isaiah 31:1-3](/bible/isaiah/31#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/isaiah/31#v1)</sup> Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/31#v2)</sup> Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/isaiah/31#v3)</sup> Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.

    Woe to them that go down to Egypt (America) for help; the Egyptians are men and not God, and when the Lord stretches out his hand both helper and helped shall fall.
